objectives: Decode taught short-/u/ CVC words using sound-by-sound blending.
Distinguish short /u/ from familiar short vowels.
Repair vowel confusions by returning to the middle grapheme and blending again.
concepts: CVC decoding requires attention to every grapheme.
Short /u/ is represented by u in the taught words.
Blending combines segmented phonemes into a spoken word.

definitions.definition: Using printed graphemes and their sounds to read a word.
Combining individual phonemes smoothly to produce a word.
A consonant-vowel-consonant word pattern such as sun.

workedExamples: cup versus cop → isolate the middle vowel, then blend again.

basic: Blend short-/u/ CVC phonemes into words.
conceptual: Explain why changing the middle vowel changes the word.
application: Decode taught-pattern CVC items without guessing.
higherOrderThinking: Identify and repair a vowel-mapping error during decoding.
mixedReview: Mix short-/u/ words with familiar short-vowel contrasts.

formulaOrFactBank: CVC decoding = grapheme recognition + phoneme production + blending
mistakeBasedRevision: If u is read as o or a, isolate the middle sound and remap printed u before blending.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat short-/u/ sound-by-sound decoding with fresh CVC words.

activities.name: Vowel repair
steps: Present a short-/u/ word and a common misread.

outcomes: Learner accurately decodes taught short-/u/ CVC words.
Learner maintains grapheme-to-phoneme accuracy across all three positions.
Learner distinguishes short /u/ from short /a/, /i/, /o/, and /e/ in controlled decoding.
Learner repairs a vowel error by returning to the middle grapheme and blending again.
